findings.where: entry hero image and related thumbnails, dom-1440
findings.evidence: The main project image has alt="Page" and the three related-project thumbnails have alt="Medium" (file-size names, not descriptions). The hero image shows 'this is a teenager by alvin chang' over a purple silhouette.
findings.after: Hero: alt="Title screen of This is a Teenager: a purple teenage silhouette on a dark background"; thumbnails: alt="" because the project title link follows each one
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 Non-text Content: the alt must convey the image's purpose, not its rendition size.

findings.evidence: Four links have empty accessible names: the hero image link to large.jpg, and the thumbnail links to /showcase/5703-gender-and-language, /5888-on-upward-mobility and /482-raw; each thumbnail link is immediately followed by a second link to the same URL with the title.
findings.after: Wrap thumbnail and title in one link, or give the image link aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"; hero link aria-label="View full-size image of This is a Teenager"
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.4 Link Purpose and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; duplicate adjacent links double the tab stops.

findings.evidence: Tab goes logo -> main nav (About … Sponsor, y 107) -> back up to the top utility bar (Twitter, Facebook, Register, Sign In, search at y 0-7). Visual order is utility bar first.
findings.before: Utility bar after main nav in DOM
findings.after: Place the utility bar before the logo in source, or use CSS order only within the same container
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.3 Focus Order and 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence.

findings.evidence: Six category links ('Longlist', 'Gold', 'Winners', 'People, Language & Identity', 'Outstanding Studio', 'Shortlist') are separated only by spacing, with no underline or separator; body links are identified by colour weight only (black on white, no underline).
findings.before: Adjacent links distinguished by whitespace only
findings.after: Render as a list (<ul>) with visible separators and underline links in content areas
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.1 Use of Color and 1.3.1 Info and Relationships.

findings.evidence: Footer link columns ('About', 'News', 'Email', 'Twitter', 'informationisbeautiful.net') are mid-grey on #50504e charcoal; visibly low contrast in the tile while the left column is white. Sweep lists 15 contrast hits; this region is consistent with them.
findings.after: Use the same near-white as the left footer column (#fff on #50504e is ~8:1)
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum). Sweep hit verified by eye.

strengths: Reflows cleanly at 375: vote panel and related projects stack under the entry with no horizontal scroll.
Primary actions are real links with clear names ('VOTE', 'VIEW ALL PROJECTS').
not_investigated: Vote flow and sign-in forms not exercised.
The two tracking pixels without alt (sweep) are 0px beacons; they should get alt="" but are not user-facing.
